ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, what is the area of the shaded part?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\[ \textbf{Solution:} \text{ Given:} \text{ The length of the shaded part is: } \sqrt{13^{2}-5^{2}}=12, \]
\[ \because \text{ the width is } 4 \text{ cm}, \]
\[ \therefore \text{ the area is: } 4\times 12=\boxed{48cm^{2}} \]

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The shaded part at the top of the figure is a rectangle, with a height of 4 cm marked on the right side. Below the rectangle there is a right triangle, with the vertical side on the left labeled 5 cm and the hypotenuse labeled 13 cm. There is a right-angle mark at the upper left corner, indicating that the vertical side and the horizontal side are perpendicular; this horizontal side is the same as the width of the shaded rectangle. Reasoning: The hypotenuse of the right triangle below is 13 cm, and one leg is 5 cm. By the Pythagorean theorem, the horizontal leg = sqrt(13^2 - 5^2) = sqrt(169 - 25) = sqrt(144) = 12 cm. Therefore, the width of the shaded rectangle is 12 cm, the height is 4 cm, and the area = 12 × 4 = 48 cm².
